question: On 28 February 2023, the European Data Protection Board (EDPB) questioned the US’s ability to protect Europeans’ personal data1. However, on 22 December 2023, Section 702 of the FISA2, which allows US intelligence agencies to access Europeans’ emails and telephone conversations3, was extended until the end of April 2024.

Furthermore, Section 504 of one of the draft reforms of the text4 – the FRRA5 – proposes to extend the scope of this law6. It sets out to expand the list of companies that can be drafted into US agencies’ service and include cross connects. Data centres (subject to US law) would also be made to install interception modules.

All of this contradicts the EUCS7, currently under negotiation8, under which the Commission wants cloud providers to be required to demonstrate legal immunity from foreign jurisdictions. The Commission had signed the DPF9, an agreement on data between the US and Europe10, on the basis that the FISA was going to be less far-reaching. 1.
What does the Commission make of this development?
Does it see an urgent need to review the DPF?

answer: In December 2023, the United States (US) Congress extended Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA, 50 US Code §1881a) without changes until April 2024, when a possible further extension will be discussed again. The Commission is closely following the developments in this regard, including whether this reauthorisation may lead to further reforms.

At the same time, it is important to point out that the necessity and proportionality safeguards that have been put in place by the Executive Order 14086 in the context of the EU-US Data Privacy Framework fully apply to surveillance under Section 702 FISA (11). The functioning and implementation of those safeguards will be assessed in the first review of the framework, which will take place in 2024 (12).
More generally, the Commission has the power to suspend, amend or repeal the adequacy decision if it concludes that the required level of protection is no longer ensured (13).
